title: Sort a sheared pile of colored sheets into trays, taking each by the edge that sticks out
instruction: Sort the stack of colored sheets: take each sheet off the stack and put it in the tray marked with the same color, and leave every sheet lying flat in its tray.
context: Sorting loose papers into trays is everyday clerical work, for example separating the white, yellow and pink copies of multipart forms: O*NET lists "Compile, copy, sort, and file records of office activities, business transactions, and other activities" and "Open, sort, and route incoming mail" for Office Clerks, General (43-9061.00, about 2.6 million US workers). A sheet lying on a pile is 0.5 mm thick and flat, so a parallel gripper cannot lift it from above. People take it by an edge that sticks out and nudge the pile to bring out the next one. The task tests that handling of thin sheets: pinching one sheet's protruding edge without taking the sheet beneath it, carrying it level, setting it down flat in a tray, and sliding the pile to expose the next sheet. Color only decides which tray; sweeping the pile off the shelf scores 0.
setup: Two YAM arms with parallel grippers, bases 61 cm apart at the near edge of a table. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, on the table: x straight out, y to the left; heights above the table. Shelf: a black box 49.6 cm long (x 11.6 to 61.2), 20 cm deep (y 7.75 to 27.75) and 15 cm tall, fixed to the table, with a slick top (PTFE film or polished laminate; card slides on it at a friction coefficient of about 0.16). Pile: four A6 sheets of 400 gsm card (14.8 x 10.5 cm, 0.5 mm thick, 6.2 g each), long side along x, centred at x 20.0 on the shelf's near end. The pile is sheared: the top sheet's right edge is at y 5.95, 1.8 cm past the shelf's right edge (y 7.75), and each sheet below lies 1.8 cm further left (right edges at y 7.75, 9.55 and 11.35). Colors from the top: pink, white, yellow, pink. Tray row: on the table along the shelf's right face, three open trays built as one unit, 49.6 cm long (x 11.6 to 61.2), from y -9.85 to y 7.55: a grey floor 4 mm thick, with grey dividers and colored outer walls 4 mm thick whose tops are 2.5 cm above the table; the shelf's face is each tray's fourth side. Each tray is 16 cm long and 17 cm deep inside, with centres at x 20.0 (yellow, below the pile), 36.4 (pink) and 52.8 (white). Each tray's outer wall is in its color, and a strip of that color, 1.2 cm wide and 1 mm thick, lies on its floor along the outer wall. Trays: smooth plastic or laminated board, fixed to the table. A second pile order is provided for a second layout, from the top: yellow, pink, white, yellow.
scoring: Measured at the end of the trial from a top photo and with a ruler. A sheet counts as in a tray when it lies flat there: seen from above, all of it is inside that tray (between the middles of its dividers, from the shelf's face to the outside of the outer wall, within 2 mm); it is tilted at most 10 degrees (one edge at most 1.8 cm higher than the opposite edge); and its lowest point is within 6 mm of the tray's floor. A sheet leaning on a wall, lying across a divider or held above the tray does not count. Score = (sheets in the tray of their own color minus sheets in a tray of another color) / 4, never below 0: 0.25 for each sheet sorted, and each sheet in a wrong tray cancels one. A sheet left on the shelf, on the table or off the table adds and subtracts nothing. 1.0 (success, which ends the trial): all four sheets in the trays of their own color and still (moving under 1 cm/s) for 1 s. Sweeping the whole pile off the shelf puts all four in the yellow tray: 1 right, 3 wrong, score 0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Take the four sheets out of the trays and rebuild the pile at the shelf's near end in the listed color order, each sheet 1.8 cm to the right of the one below and the top sheet's edge 1.8 cm past the shelf's edge. Wipe the shelf's top if it has picked up dust.
fidelity: Each sheet is a rigid plate the size and weight of A6 400 gsm card; it does not bend, crease or flutter (air drag is modelled as damping). Friction: card on card 0.30 static and 0.25 kinetic, card on the shelf's top 0.16 and 0.135, finger pad on card 0.40 and 0.375. The shelf and trays are fixed. Card is used because thin office paper is too floppy to model as a rigid plate.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps; the left arm pushed the whole pile off the shelf into the yellow tray by about 45 s, and no sheet was pinched); demo: 1.0 (success at step 941)
